# Tall stature

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Surgery > Pediatric surgery > Tall stature*

[Original Article Link](/library/1402RT)

---

## Summary

Tall stature is defined as a height of more than 2 <u>standard deviations</u> (SDs) above the population mean or exceeding the 97th <u>percentile</u> for age and sex. Most tall stature is due to physiological causes (e.g., familial tall stature, <u>constitutional advancement of growth</u>). However, tall stature can also be caused by an underlying endocrine or genetic condition. The clinical evaluation of tall stature includes a thorough <u>medical history</u> (including developmental history and <u>family history</u>), an <u>assessment of pediatric growth</u> and <u>growth velocity</u>, and identification of signs of <u>puberty</u> or dysmorphic features. Diagnostics include a determination of <u>bone age</u> in all children. If an endocrine or genetic cause is suspected, a referral to a pediatric specialist is recommended for additional studies (e.g., hormonal and/or genetic studies) and/or management. In tall stature due to physiological causes, management is limited to reassurance and regular growth monitoring.

---

## Etiology

### Physiological causes [[1]](/library/Nxd-9H0)[[2]](/library/6CdjGH0)




* Familial tall stature

* <u>Constitutional advancement of growth</u>





### Endocrine causes [[1]](/library/Nxd-9H0)[[2]](/library/6CdjGH0)




* <u>Obesity</u>

* <u>Precocious puberty</u>

* <u>Hyperthyroidism</u>

* <u>Growth hormone</u> excess (e.g., <u>pituitary gigantism</u>)





### Genetic causes [[1]](/library/Nxd-9H0)[[2]](/library/6CdjGH0)




* <u>Chromosomal abnormalities</u>, e.g.:

* <u>Klinefelter syndrome</u> (<u>47,XXY</u>)

* <u>47,XYY syndrome</u>

* <u>47,XXX syndrome</u>

* <u>Fragile X syndrome</u>

* <u>Marfan syndrome</u>

* <u>Overgrowth syndromes</u>, e.g.:

* <u>Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome</u>

* <u>Sotos syndrome</u> (<u>cerebral gigantism</u>)

* Weaver syndrome

* <u>Proteus syndrome</u>

* <u>Primary male hypogonadism</u> [[3]](/library/oCd0GH0)[[4]](/library/jxd_wH0)

* <u>Homocystinuria</u>

* <u>Estrogen deficiency</u> (e.g., due to <u>aromatase deficiency</u>) or resistance [[5]](/library/KCdUGH0)

* <u>Androgen</u> insensitivity

* Familial <u>glucocorticoid</u> deficiency [[5]](/library/KCdUGH0)

---

## Clinical evaluation

### Focused history [[2]](/library/6CdjGH0)[[3]](/library/oCd0GH0)




* Onset: recent accelerated growth  [[3]](/library/oCd0GH0)

* Developmental history

* Delay in <u>developmental milestones</u>

* Early or <u>precocious puberty</u>

* Associated signs and symptoms

* <u>Signs of hyperthyroidism</u>

* Signs of <u>mass effect</u> from a <u>pituitary adenoma</u> (e.g., <u>headaches</u> and <u>vision</u> changes)

* <u>Family history</u>

* Tall stature

* Genetic disorders and associated findings

* Endocrine disorders (e.g., <u>Graves disease</u>)





> [!WARNING]
> In tall children whose height is within the expected range, in addition to physiological causes, consider undiagnosed underlying familial conditions (e.g., <u>Marfan syndrome</u>). [[3]](/library/oCd0GH0)




### Focused <u>physical examination</u> [[1]](/library/Nxd-9H0)[[2]](/library/6CdjGH0)[[3]](/library/oCd0GH0)




* Growth assessment

* Standard <u>pediatric growth</u> assessment, including:

* Growth parameters (e.g., length, height, weight, head circumference) plotted on appropriate growth charts

* <u>Midparental height</u> calculation

* <u>Growth velocity</u>

* General <u>physical examination</u>

* <u>Secondary sexual characteristics</u>: for evidence of early or <u>precocious puberty</u>

* Proportionality assessment (e.g., arm span, sitting vs. standing height)

* <u>Thyroid examination</u>

* Dysmorphic features

---

## Diagnostics

* All patients: <u>bone age</u>  [[1]](/library/Nxd-9H0)[[3]](/library/oCd0GH0)

* Select patients: Refer to a pediatric specialist (e.g., <u>endocrinology</u>, genetics) for additional diagnostic studies. [[1]](/library/Nxd-9H0)[[2]](/library/6CdjGH0)

* Endocrine laboratory tests, e.g.:

* <u>Thyroid function tests</u>

* <u>FSH</u>, <u>LH</u>, <u>testosterone</u> (boys), <u>estradiol</u> (girls): for <u>precocious puberty</u>

* <u>Hyperglycemia tests</u>  [[1]](/library/Nxd-9H0)

* <u>Insulin-like growth factor 1</u>: for suspected <u>gigantism</u>

* Genetic studies (e.g., <u>karyotyping</u>)

* <u>MRI</u> <u>brain</u>: for suspected <u>pituitary adenoma</u>

## Common causes

### Physiological and endocrine causes




| <br>Common physiological and endocrine <u>causes of tall stature</u> [[1]](/library/Nxd-9H0)<br> |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Condition | Characteristic clinical features | Diagnostic findings | Management |
| Familial tall stature | <br><br>* <u>Family history</u> of tall stature<br><br>* Projected height within 2 SDs of <u>midparental height</u> [[1]](/library/Nxd-9H0)<br><br><br> | <br>* Normal <u>bone age</u><br><br> | <br><br>* Reassurance<br><br>* Regular growth monitoring<br><br><br> |
| <u>Constitutional advancement of growth</u> | <br><br>* Accelerated growth before 4 years of age, then normal <u>growth velocity</u> until <u>puberty</u><br><br>* Early or <u>precocious puberty</u>  [[1]](/library/Nxd-9H0)<br><br>* Normal adult height<br><br><br> | <br>* Advanced <u>bone age</u><br><br> | <br><br>* Reassurance<br><br>* Regular growth monitoring<br><br><br> |
| <u>Obesity</u> | <br><br>* ↑ <u>BMI</u><br><br>* Early or <u>precocious puberty</u><br><br>* Normal adult height<br><br><br> | <br>* Advanced <u>bone age</u><br><br> | <br>* See “<u>Overweight and obesity in children</u>.”<br><br> |
| <br><u>Precocious puberty</u> [[6]](/library/IodYWI0)<br> | <br><br>* Early onset of <u>secondary sexual characteristics</u><br><br>* <u>♀</u>: before 8 years of age<br><br>* <u>♂</u>: before 9 years of age<br><br>* Reduced <u>growth velocity</u> over time → shorter adult height<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Advanced <u>bone age</u><br><br>* Abnormal <u>LH</u>, <u>FSH</u>, <u>estradiol</u>, <u>testosterone</u>, 17 alpha-hydroxyprogesterone<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Treatment of underlying cause<br><br>* <u>GnRH agonists</u> for <u>central precocious puberty</u><br><br><br> |
| <u>Hyperthyroidism</u> | <br><br>* <u>Symptoms of hyperthyroidism</u><br><br>* Abnormal <u>thyroid examination</u> (e.g., <u>thyromegaly</u>)<br><br>* Projected height > 2 SDs of <u>midparental height</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* ↓ <u>TSH</u><br><br>* ↑ Free T4<br><br><br> | <br>* See “<u>Graves disease in children</u>.”<br><br> |
| <br><u>Pituitary gigantism</u> [[7]](/library/TBb6Zw)<br> | <br><br>* Coarse facial features, <u>frontal bossing</u>, <u>prognathism</u><br><br>* Enlarged hands and feet<br><br>* <u>Hypertension</u>, <u>hyperhidrosis</u><br><br>* Projected height > 2 SDs of <u>midparental height</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* ↑ Serum <u>IGF-1</u><br><br>* Lack of <u>GH</u> suppression after oral <u>glucose</u> test<br><br>* <u>MRI</u> <u>brain</u>: <u>pituitary adenoma</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Surgery</u><br><br>* Medical therapy (<u>somatostatin receptor ligands</u>, <u>GH receptor antagonists</u>)<br><br>* <u>Radiation therapy</u><br><br><br> |





### Genetic causes




| Common genetic <u>causes of tall stature</u> |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Condition |  | Characteristic clinical features | Diagnostic findings | Management |
| <br><u>Sex chromosome</u> <u>aneuploidy</u> [[2]](/library/6CdjGH0)[[8]](/library/LxdwCH0)<br> | <br><u>Klinefelter syndrome</u>  [[9]](/library/MxdMCH0)<br> | <br><br>* <u>Gynecomastia</u><br><br>* <u>Delayed puberty</u>, testicular <u>hypoplasia</u><br><br>* <u>Infertility</u><br><br>* <u>Neurodevelopmental disorders</u><br><br>* Disproportionate growth<br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Karyotype</u>: <u>47,XXY</u><br><br>* Laboratory findings of <u>primary male hypogonadism</u><br><br>* ↑ <u>FSH</u> and <u>LH</u><br><br>* ↓ <u>Testosterone</u><br><br><br> | <br>* Treatment of disease manifestations, e.g.:<br><br>* <u>Management of male hypogonadism</u><br><br>* <u>Management of primary ovarian insufficiency</u><br><br>* <u>Treatment of infertility</u><br><br>* Educational support and developmental therapies<br><br> |
| <br>47,XYY syndrome or <u>47,XXX</u> syndrome<br> | <br><br>* Tall stature may be only feature<br><br>* <u>Neurodevelopmental disorders</u><br><br>* <u>Pubertal development</u> and <u>fertility</u> usually normal<br><br>* <u>Hypotonia</u> (<u>47,XXX syndrome</u>)<br><br><br> | <br>* <u>Karyotype</u> confirming specific <u>aneuploidy</u><br><br> |  |  |
| <br><u>Fragile X syndrome</u>  [[10]](/library/6xdjxH0)<br> |  | <br><br>* Large <u>ears</u>, high-arched <u>palate</u>, long face<br><br>* <u>Macroorchidism</u><br><br>* <u>Pes planus</u><br><br>* <u>Developmental delay</u><br><br><br> | <br>* FMR1 <u>gene</u> variant<br><br> | <br>* Symptom management (e.g., developmental and behavioral therapies)<br><br> |
| <br><u>Marfan syndrome</u>  [[11]](/library/mxdVCH0)<br> |  | <br><br>* <u>Marfanoid habitus</u> with disproportionately long extremities<br><br>* <u>Kyphoscoliosis</u><br><br>* <u>Sternum</u> deformities (e.g., <u>pectus excavatum</u>)<br><br><br> | <br>* Positive <u>revised Ghent criteria</u><br><br>* <u>Echocardiogram</u>: <u>aortic root dilatation</u><br><br>* Ophthalmologic examination: superior <u>ectopia lentis</u><br><br>* <u>FBN1</u> <u>gene</u> variant<br><br> | <br><br>* Regular cardiac and ophthalmologic monitoring<br><br>* <u>Surgery</u> referral as needed for musculoskeletal complications<br><br><br> |
| <br><u>Homocystinuria</u>  [[12]](/library/oxd0xH0)<br> |  | <br><br>* <u>Marfanoid habitus</u><br><br>* <u>Developmental delay</u><br><br>* <u>Thromboembolic events</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* ↑ Serum <u>homocysteine</u> and <u>methionine</u><br><br>* Ophthalmologic examination: inferior <u>ectopia lentis</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Vitamin B<sub>6</sub></u> supplementation<br><br>* Dietary <u>methionine</u> restriction<br><br><br> |
| <u>Overgrowth syndromes</u> | <br><u>Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome</u>  [[13]](/library/KxdUxH0)<br> | <br><br>* <u>Macrosomia</u><br><br>* <u>Macroglossia</u><br><br>* <u>Omphalocele</u><br><br>* <u>Hemihyperplasia</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Advanced <u>bone age</u><br><br>* <u>Genetic testing</u>: 11p15.5 <u>chromosomal abnormality</u><br><br>* Laboratory <u>findings consistent with endogenous hyperinsulinism</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Abdominal <u>ultrasound</u> surveillance for embryonal tumors<br><br>* Management of specific features, e.g.:<br><br>* <u>Management of hypoglycemia</u><br><br>* <u>Surgery</u> if indicated for <u>macroglossia</u><br><br><br> |
| <br><u>Sotos syndrome</u>  [[14]](/library/KwdUPH0)[[15]](/library/6wdjPH0)<br> | <br><br>* <u>Macrocephaly</u><br><br>* Dysmorphic facial features (e.g., elongated face, prominent narrow <u>jaw</u>)<br><br>* Feeding difficulties, <u>hypotonia</u><br><br>* <u>Developmental delay</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* NSD1 <u>gene</u> variant<br><br>* Advanced <u>bone age</u><br><br>* Cardiac and/or renal abnormalities may be visible on imaging. [[16]](/library/nxd7CH0)<br><br><br> | <br>* Symptom management, e.g:<br><br>* Educational support and developmental therapies<br><br>* <u>Nutritional support</u><br><br> |  |
| <br>Weaver syndrome [[14]](/library/KwdUPH0)<br> | <br><br>* <u>Micrognathia</u>, broad forehead<br><br>* <u>Hypertelorism</u><br><br>* <u>Camptodactyly</u><br><br>* <u>Intellectual disability</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Advanced <u>bone age</u><br><br>* EZH2 <u>gene</u> variant<br><br><br> | <br>* Monitoring for and treatment of associated conditions (e.g., <u>malignancy</u>)<br><br> |  |
